cause.label: dilution_or_going_concern
cause.what_happened: After the close on Thu 2026-09-24 (16:05 ET) Car-Mart filed an 8-K. It said Silver Point and the lenders had extended the covenant waiver on minimum liquidity and collateral coverage by only one more week, to 2026-10-01. That was the fourth short extension since 2026-09-04. The filing also warned that shareholders could suffer a 'significant or complete loss' and that the company may need bankruptcy protection. On Fri 2026-09-25 the stock opened +2.9% and then sold off 21.8% intraday to about $1.10, on 3.4x normal volume. This was the second straight day down about 19%.

evidence.claim: The waiver and temporary relief were extended through 2026-10-01. The filing says 'holders of the Company's common stock could experience a significant or complete loss of their investment' and lists 'the potential need to seek protection under applicable bankruptcy or insolvency laws' as a risk. The company 'believes it has made significant progress towards a transaction'.
The earlier extensions ran from 09-07 to 09-11, then 09-18, then 09-24. Each was a weekly roll, filed as its own 8-K.
On 2026-09-24 the shares fell 19% to a 52-week low ahead of the creditor deadline. Q1 figures: unrestricted cash $27.5m, total debt $623.9m, Q1 loss $69m. Houlihan Lokey is advising.

The June amendment had set the waiver period to early September, with a possible extension to November 2026 if certain conditions were met. The weekly rolls since then mean that longer extension was not granted.
Shares outstanding were 8,663,493 at the 2026-07-31 record date. At about $1.10 that is roughly $9.5m of equity against $623.9m of debt.

pipeline.next_dated_event: The Silver Point waiver and temporary covenant relief expire on 2026-10-01 (per the 8-K filed 2026-09-24). That is three sessions after the window closes.
pipeline.what_would_change_my_mind: An 8-K or press release dated on or before 2026-09-28 would change this. A signed transaction that gives the common stock value would be a positive finding. A Chapter 11 petition or restructuring support agreement filed over the 09-26/27 weekend would be a large negative one. Neither is dated or sourced as of the screen.

positioning_check: Short interest was 1,592,970 shares at the 2026-09-15 settlement, 1.78 days to cover on 893,509 average daily volume, up 10.0% from 1,448,088 at 2026-08-31 (https://api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/CRMT/short-interest?assetclass=stocks). That is about 18.4% of the 8,663,493 shares outstanding (5.07 8-K, record date 2026-07-31). The figure is ten days and two -19% sessions stale, so the position carried into this fall is not observable. There is no options market (baseline options.status no_options_market), so there is no skew to read.

outside_window.finding: The lender waiver and covenant relief expire on 2026-10-01. By then the company must produce a transaction, another short extension, or a filing. The 8-K flags bankruptcy protection and a possible complete loss for the common stock. The equity is about $9.5m against $623.9m of debt, with a $300m Silver Point senior loan, so a restructuring outcome is skewed hard against the common. The 'significant progress towards a transaction' language is the only upside path. This is the second shoe, but it is dated after the window closes.
Rosen Law Firm has announced a securities class-action investigation, following the 2026-09-09 Q1 print that dropped the stock 41.8%. No complaint or docket was located and no date is set.

searched_and_found_nothing: Open ATM or shelf takedown. EFTS full-text search for 'at-the-market' in CIK 799850 from 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-25 returned only the January 2026 S-1/424B3. That is a selling-stockholder resale of 937,487 Silver Point/Beach Point warrant shares at a $22.63 strike, deep out of the money. There is no primary ATM and no supply that can price tonight. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/799850/000110465926004576/tm2534619d2_424b3.htm

Disclosed buyer. The four Form 4s filed 2026-09-25 are option grants (code A, $7.37 strike, vesting from 2027) triggered by the 09-23 plan-amendment vote. They are not open-market purchases and not a buyer under the stock. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/799850/000168316826007421/xslF345X06/ownership.xml and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/799850/000168316826007427/xslF345X06/ownership.xml

Reverse split or bid-price deficiency. The 2026-09-23 annual-meeting 8-K (Item 5.07) had no reverse-split proposal. The price is still above $1, so no 30-day deficiency clock can have started. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/799850/000117184326006214/f8k_092426.htm

A wire story contradicted by the document. The 09-24 8-K itself carries the complete-loss and bankruptcy language, so the tape was not trading a headline the primary document refutes. There is no repricing mechanism.
A scheduled release, payment date or hearing inside 2026-09-25 to 2026-09-28. None was found in the 8-Ks of 09-04, 09-11, 09-18 or 09-24. The only dated item is the 2026-10-01 waiver expiry.
